source_audit: Local Mathlib primary APIs for dense Schwartz-to-Lp range, continuity from dense fibers and uniform Lipschitz control, matrix group topology, strongly measurable continuous functions, Bochner integration and multiplicative convolution of measures. Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, Section 3 Claims 3.3–3.4, equation (3.2) and Proposition 3.5 (https://arxiv.org/html/1108.2555#S3), re-read in R1777. R1777 proves pairwise comparison, joint continuity, integrable probability averages and exact right-convolution smoothing in the representation convention T_g=W_(g^-1). The error bound is independent of the original measure support, by contraction and the exact convolution identity. The finite generator-measure bridge, dyadic power lower bound, concrete Haar kernel and asymptotic parameter choice are still explicit obligations. No novelty claimed for standard representation or analytic support.

proof_scope: In progress. R1777 extends the local perturbation bound to pairs g,h with arbitrary reference-entry bound B: if |h_ik|<=B, |g_ik-h_ik|<=eta and 2*B*eta<=1/2, then ||W_g u-W_h u||<=58*B*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta for Q_j(u)<=R. The B=2 case gives constant 116. This proves continuity of every Schwartz orbit, and density plus isometry proves joint continuity on actual complex L2 times SL(2,R). Finite Borel measures give integrable actual representation orbits T_g=W_(g^-1). Their Bochner averages contract for probability measures and satisfy the exact convolution identity A_(mu*nu)=A_mu o A_nu. Consequently right-convolution smoothing changes A_mu u by at most ||A_nu u-u||, and by at most 29*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta for a kernel nu supported almost everywhere in the stated near-identity entry neighborhood. The error is independent of mu's support size or word length. A corresponding half-norm lower bound is proved whenever the error is at most half a known original lower bound.
